correctness.rationale: For multiplicative beta(p^a)=(p^(a+1)+(-1)^a)/(p+1), beta(m)<m when m>1 and beta(pq)=(p-1)(q-1) for distinct primes. If beta(n)=beta(n+1) and Omega(n),Omega(n+1)<=2, n+1 cannot be prime; n prime also excluded by elementary cases. Both composite force even member 2q (q odd prime), beta=q-1, and odd neighbor either r^2 or rs (odd primes); matching values with adjacency yields impossible r^2-2r+3=0 or r^2-2r+5=0, or (r-2)(s-2)=1 with r=s=3 contrary to distinctness, or (r-2)(s-2)=-1. Thus n=1 uniquely, and n=20 attains sharp multiplicity Omega(20)=3, Omega(21)=2 and beta values 12. Independently enumerated n<10000 as corroboration, not an infinite proof; actual source verify.py independently enumerates n<2 million.
residual_risks: An unindexed elementary characterization of low-Omega consecutive beta equalities might predate this argument.
